questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Are you looking forward ______ Nikhil again?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is **'****to seeing'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this case “to” is a **preposition**, and you always need to use the ‘ing’ form **(gerund)** after a **preposition**.
 
• ‘looking forward’ is a** phrasal verb**. A phrasal verb contains a **verb **and a **preposition** and in this case, two prepositions (forward and to).
 
• To look forward to is a** transitive verb** which means that it needs an **object** ( a noun or a verb).
 
• As ‘seeing’ is a **gerund** (noun form of verb), the answer should be 'to seeing'.
 
• This option uses the gerund form "seeing" after the preposition "to." It is the most appropriate choice as it maintains parallel structure and conveys the idea of anticipation or expectation. "Looking forward to seeing" is a common phrase used to express excitement about a future event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Are you looking forward *to seeing*__ Nikhil again?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **seeing**

 
 
• This option uses the gerund form "seeing" as the object of the verb "looking forward." While gerunds can function as nouns, in this context, it feels incomplete. "Looking forward" is typically followed by a preposition such as "to" to indicate what is being anticipated.
 
 
 
• **to see**
 
 
• This option uses the infinitive form "to see" as the object of the verb "looking forward." The infinitive form is commonly used after "looking forward" to express anticipation or expectation. It is a valid choice and grammatically correct.
 
 
 
• **to be seeing**
 
 
• This option uses the present progressive form "to be seeing" as the object of the verb "looking forward." However, using the present progressive form in this context suggests ongoing or continuous action, which may not be appropriate. "Looking forward" implies anticipation of a specific event or action, rather than an ongoing process.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

He opened the door for his mother.

options.text: The door was opened by him for his mother.
The door was open by him for his mother.
The door had been opened by him for his mother.
The door is opened by him for his mother.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** '​****The door was opened by him for his mother'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V₂ + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V₃ + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'He'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the door'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'opened' will be changed into 'was opened'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added. 

 

Correct Sentence:__ *The door was opened by him for his mother.*

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. The interest rates offered depends on the bank, deposit amount and the tenure you choose.

B. It not only helps you to save money but also helps you to earn a substantial interest on it.

C. One of the best ways to secure your money is by investing in fixed deposits.

D. Under the fixed deposit scheme, the depositor deposits the money only once at the time of opening the account.
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is '**CDBA**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'.
 
 
• **Sentence C** will be the first sentence because it is an independent introductory sentence that tells us about the fixed deposits.
 
• **Sentence D** will be the next sentence because it explains what is a fixed deposit.
 
• **Sentence B** will be used afterward because it is connected with the previous sentence.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence A** will be used.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is:
 
 
• **C**: One of the best ways to secure your money is by investing in fixed deposits.
 
• **D**: Under the fixed deposit scheme, the depositor deposits the money only once at the time of opening the account.
 
• **B**: It not only helps you to save money but also helps you to earn a substantial interest on it.
 
• **A**: The interest rates offered depends on the bank, deposit amount and the tenure you choose.

 
 
 
 
 

**Correct Sequence:__** *One of the best ways to secure your money is by investing in fixed deposits. Under the fixed deposit scheme, the depositor deposits the money only once at the time of opening the account. It not only helps you to save money but also helps you to earn a substantial interest on it. The interest rates offered depends on the bank, deposit amount and the tenure you choose.*
